title: SS27 Men's Pyjama Polish
summary: Sleepwear turns into city wear: long tunic shirts, piped two-piece sets and check sets with matching coats, made luxurious.

sections.heading: The story
sections.body: Dior lengthened sleepwear into knee-length tunics and showed two-piece sets in khaki, blue and beige with black collars and piping; Sarah Burton's first menswear collection for Givenchy included a buttoned beige and blue check two-piece with a matching coat<sup>[1]</sup>. Alice Feillard, director of menswear buying at Galeries Lafayette, described "a pyjama effect, but a rather sophisticated, luxurious one"<sup>[1]</sup>. Hypebeast also suggested pajama-style dressing in satin<sup>[2]</sup>, and monochrome sets of long-sleeve tops with wide trousers appeared at IM Men and Celine<sup>[3]</sup>.

sections.heading: Colours
sections.body: Khaki, blue and beige with black piping; sand and ice blue from the SS27 menswear palette.

sections.heading: Silhouettes
sections.body:
- Two-piece sets: camp-collar or tunic shirt with drawstring or wide trousers.
- Knee-length tunic shirts.
- Set with matching coat.

sections.heading: Fabrics
sections.body: Poplin, satin, check shirting, seersucker, fine cotton and silk blends.

sections.heading: Trims and details
sections.body: Contrast collars and piping, covered buttons, drawstrings, patch pockets.

timing: In stores February to July 2027. Rising; suits resort and holiday drops.
products: - Two-piece sets, tunic shirts, set-plus-coat looks; sold as separates and as sets.
design_implications:
- Piping and contrast collars carry the idea: specify them carefully.
- Cut set trousers with a fly and proper waistband so they work as city trousers.
commercial_implications:
- Price sets to reward buying both pieces.
- Good for resort and holiday markets (Gulf, India, Southeast Asia).
